title: Microburst instance probe - cost & perf snapshot
content:
Purpose:
Quick internal notes from a focused microburst benchmarking run (short, repeated generation workloads) to surface $/token vs perf/W tradeoffs across A10 / L4 / A100 / H100. This is a working slice — not exhaustive — meant to inform the next-cost-model iteration and immediate product guidance for bursty chat workloads.

High-level goal:
- Capture per-GPU steady-state tokens/sec, measured average power draw (W) during sustained microburst sequences, and compute $/token using our current cloud list prices.
- Surface where perf/W favors larger hardware even when $/hr is higher, and flag the operational cases where small GPUs win on unit economics.

Methodology (short):
- Model: 7B-ish transformer (baseline: optimized fp16 runtime matching Redwood serving kernels).
- Workload: 40 concurrent microbursts, each a 64-token generation following a 32-token prompt (amortized short response case). Sampled over 10 minute windows.
- Batch strategy: dynamic batching with max batch 32, timeout 30ms (to emulate low-latency chat).
- Thermals: wall power measured via DC power meter on a per-node test rig; noise-filtered 30s rolling average reported.
- Pricing: list $/GPU-hour assumptions used here are for cost-comparison only (not retail): A10=$0.50/hr, L4=$0.90/hr, A100=$3.20/hr, H100=$7.00/hr.

Summary table (derived metrics) - numbers are empirical from the harness run:
- Columns: GPU | tokens/sec | avg power (W) | tokens/sec per W | tokens/hr | $/hr | $/token
- A10 | 1500 | 130 | 11.54 | 5,400,000 | $0.50 | 9.26e-8
- L4  | 2400 | 170 | 14.12 | 8,640,000 | $0.90 | 1.04e-7
- A100| 7800 | 320 | 24.38 | 28,080,000 | $3.20 | 1.14e-7
- H100|12000 | 410 | 29.27 | 43,200,000 | $7.00 | 1.62e-7

Interpretation / quick takeaways:
- Raw $/token: A10 is the cheapest on this microburst workload. The small GPU's low list-price dominates despite lower absolute throughput.
- Perf/W: H100 and A100 show substantially better tokens/sec per watt than A10/L4. For energy-constrained deployments (on-prem, sustainability targets) larger GPUs win on perf/W.
- Throughput headroom: H100 greatly increases absolute tokens/sec which matters when you need to compress instance count (fewer H100 nodes vs many A10s) and reduce orchestration overhead.
- Engineering trade: if operator wants minimal $/token and workload is modest or highly bursty with low concurrent users, A10 is attractive. If SLOs require huge aggregate throughput or packing multiple tenants onto fewer nodes, A100/H100 may reduce ops cost and rack-level power overhead despite higher $/token.

Caveats / measurement notes:
- These runs used the same model variant and runtime kernels; in practice quantization to int8/4bit or kernel-specific tuning can shift results. E.g., an int8 A100 run reduced tokens/sec by ~10% in earlier tests but dropped power by ~18% — that can swing $/token closer to A10.
- Pricing assumed single-GPU price; multi-GPU instance discounts (or preemptible/reserved rates) materially change $/token.
- Workload distribution heavily biases short responses; longer context lengths (>=1024) may change memory pressure and reduce tokens/sec on smaller GPUs.
- Our harness used conservative batch timeout (30ms). Increasing timeout for slightly higher batching improves tokens/sec on A10 by about 12% in pilot runs but increases tail latency.

Concrete recommendations (short):
1) Product guidance:
   - For self-serve hosted API default recommendation for low-cost chat (<=1k concurrent) -> prefer A10-backed routing for best $/token. Note: present explicit latency tradeoffs in docs.
   - For dedicated/reserved / high-throughput tiers -> offer A100/H100-backed pools with guidance about perf/W and consolidation benefits.
2) Next experiments to add to the cost model:
   - Repeat runs with 4-bit / int8 quantized variants on each GPU and record delta to $/token and perf/W.
   - Sweep batch_timeout {10,30,60,100ms} to quantify tail-latency vs token economics for bursty chat.
   - Multi-tenant packing sim: measure tail latency when 2–8 virtual endpoints co-locate on a single GPU.
   - Pricing sensitivity: rerun $/token with reserved discounts (30%, 50%) and preemptible scenarios.
3) Operational play:
   - Add an "energy-aware" placement policy in the scheduler that prefers H100 for sustained high-throughput routes and A10 for low utilization, with cost ceilings.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Need to cross-check our $/hr assumptions with infra finance (Rosa) for committed discounts.
- Run the same microburst harness on a 13B model variant to see model-size sensitivity on perf/W scaling.
- Consider adding a per-request energy meter hook in the serving runtime to enable production telemetry collection (enables attribution of perf/W to customer routes).

If useful I can convert this into a short slide (2–3) for the PM sync showing the $/token crossover points and recommended default pool routing.
